title: MNS sends toy Toyota Innovas to BMC commissioner over vehicle upgrade row
content: A controversial BMC proposal to replace its Scorpio SUVs with newer Toyota Innovas has drawn criticism. In protest, MNS leaders sent toy Innovas to the BMC Commissioner as a symbolic gesture. Opposition parties have challenged the funding and timing of the fleet refresh, while the ruling BJP maintains the change was a collective decision. Calls for retaining the Scorpios for uniformity in the fleet persist.

title: Lauren Sanchez worked at waterpark; 40 years later, she takes luxurious ocean trips

The Bezos Earth Fund supports significant conservation projects in the Galápagos Marine Reserve. This funding protects vital habitats and migration routes for numerous marine species. Sanchez's work now focuses on protecting vast Pacific waters and their ecosystems.

title: 'Go on hunger strike, face lathi, then I'll resign': Kharge Jr. on students' stir

title: Four dangerous fish bacteria found in Brazil; one jumps to new host
content: For the first time, Brazil faces a significant challenge as bacteria previously exclusive to Asia and the USA have been identified within its borders. These bacteria, known to cause columnaris disease, pose an acute risk to the thriving aquaculture sector. Researchers have isolated four species from the Flavobacterium genus, which can infect both Nile tilapia and indigenous fish species.

title: Indian techie in Ireland explains why many who move abroad never return
content: An Indian tech professional settled in Ireland shared insights on why many expatriates choose not to return home. He emphasized Ireland's exceptional quality of life and optimal work-life balance, where staff can truly unplug after hours to indulge in hobbies and the tranquility of nature. This lifestyle, despite the challenges of high taxes and housing, is considered a worthwhile trade-off for personal development by many Indians living overseas.

title: Multiple WhatsApp accounts put under review: Reasons, how to appeal & more
content: Meta-owned WhatsApp has placed numerous accounts under a 24-hour review process. Users reported seeing a message indicating their account activity is being checked. This temporary ban prevents access to all app features and chat history. Users can submit a review request if they believe the ban is an error. WhatsApp states that violations of its terms of service lead to account bans.

title: As France sees its first fire cloud, should India be worried?
content: France witnessed its first pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud event in July 2026.  This phenomenon occurs when intense wildfires create their own thunderstorms.  India's rising temperatures and dry spells increase forest fire frequency.  While India has not reported fire clouds, its forests are becoming more flammable.  The Himalayan pine belt presents the highest potential for such an event in India.

title: Centre moves Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, proposes major reforms
content: The government has unveiled a progressive bill introducing substantial tax reforms and incentives designed to stimulate investment and enhance the electronics manufacturing sector. Key features include extended tax exemptions for capital goods supplied to local manufacturers and streamlined digital payment regulations. Furthermore, it aims to provide relief to business trusts while replacing an existing ordinance and ensuring consultations with stakeholders are integrated into the legislative process.

title: Triple murder? 3 deaf-mute rag pickers found dead in rented room in UP

Initial investigations suggest a possible internal conflict led to their tragic deaths. The landlord and neighbors could not provide definitive identification for the victims. Further investigations are currently underway to determine the exact cause of death.

title: Haryana wins medals, Gujarat wins projects: Hooda's swipe over CWG 2030 host pick

Hooda stated that Haryana has secured over fifty percent of India's medals. He urged the government to invest sports infrastructure in Haryana. The MP also criticized the concentration of projects in Gujarat.

title: From sugar subsidies to PLI schemes, here's what New Delhi is defending at WTO
content: India currently defends nine trade disputes at the World Trade Organization.  The government has spent approximately Rs 2.43 crore on legal services for these cases.  Japan, China, the EU, Brazil, and Australia are among the challenging countries.  Disputes involve steel imports, sugar support, and ICT tariffs.  China also challenges India's production-linked incentive schemes and technology measures.

title: Scientists warn Earth could hit the 1.5°C climate limit sooner than expected
content: Global warming has significantly accelerated, with the past decade warming faster than any comparable period. Researchers removed natural climate fluctuations to reveal this underlying warming trend. Five major global temperature datasets confirm this acceleration with high statistical confidence. This observed increase suggests the world may approach key climate thresholds sooner. The long-term trend could cross the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C limit before this decade ends.

title: Bakery told to pay Rs 15,160 for selling expired Diet Coke tins to customer

The bakery owner attempted to bribe the customer to conceal the expired product. The commission ruled the seller, not Coca-Cola India, is liable for such sales. Startups must integrate privacy into operations before the May 2027 deadline.
